description_full: Charter Communications, Inc. operates as a broadband connectivity company in the United States. The company offers subscription-based internet, mobile, video, and voice services; broadband connectivity services, including fixed internet, WiFi, and mobile; Spectrum internet products; advanced WiFi services; and in-home WiFi, which provides customers with high performance wireless routers and managed WiFi services to enhance their wireless internet experience. It also offers wireline voice communications services using voice over internet protocol technology; Call Guard, an advanced caller ID and robocall blocking solution; video programming and video services, including access to an interactive programming guide with parental controls, video on demand and pay-per-view services; and broadband communications solutions, such as internet access, data networking, fiber connectivity, video entertainment, and business telephone services. In addition, the company provides advertising services on cable television networks, various streaming services, and advertising platforms for local, regional and national businesses. Further, it offers production and technical services for regional sports networks; owns and manages local news channels, including Spectrum News NY1® and Spectrum News SoCal; and delivers broadband connectivity solutions to apartments, single-family gated communities, off-campus student housing, senior residences, and RV parks. The company was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.

financial_summary: Charter Communications, Inc. is a large-cap communication services business with a $15.3B market cap on $54.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years and +19% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $4.4B in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.22× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.4× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 33.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 3.1% of the shares.

hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.4x net debt to EBITDA ($477.0M of cash against $94.8B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.6x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.59 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.39 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 0.5% over 3 years, 2.6% over 5 years and 18.8% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 56%).
At current returns, reinvesting 40% of profits supports about 3.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -9.2% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.3x, 21.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
